messages:
Nora (AE): Urgent: customer POC failing — function_call + json_mode=strict returns malformed JSON intermittently and they also hit 429s under load. Need quick unblock for tomorrow midday exec demo.
Sam (Solutions): Customer says: 'payloads sometimes end with a trailing comma or cut off mid-object. Also getting 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining:0 when ramping to ~30 parallel clients.'
Ivy (Runtime): Please paste a sanitized request/response and x-request-id. Also confirm model and streaming flag.
Nora (AE): Sent: model=redwood-large-v2, streaming=false, max_tokens=1600. Example RESP 200 body: "{\"id\":\"tx-5\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"amount\":100, }" then later RESP 429 header x-request-id: demo-321 x-rate-limit-remaining:0.
Lee (Oncall): Likely two issues: (1) serializer chunking -> truncated output; (2) burst throttle. Immediate mitigations: reduce concurrency to <=10, enable jittered exponential backoff.
Sam (Solutions): Short-term fixes to propose now: set json_mode to "lax", reduce max_tokens, or enable streaming=true and assemble chunks client-side (we can share a tiny reassembly helper). If they insist on 30 concurrent for demo, request a temporary per-key QPS bump.
Security Bot: Note: per-key tolerant parsing raises risk. Approval required (demo key, TTL <= 6h, audit logs).
Ivy (Runtime): If Security ok I can enable tolerant parser for their key for 4h and log tolerant parses. Lee can bump QPS 25->50 for 2h. Need exact x-request-id(s) to correlate logs.
Nora (AE): Action items: 1) Ask customer to drop concurrency and add jitter now. 2) Customer to repro and share x-request-id(s). 3) Ivy/Lee prepare tolerant-parser + QPS bump plan pending Security. 4) Sam to draft Dedicated/Private cost sketch for follow-up. I'll update when I have ids. :thumbsup:
